bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Pay: Hourly to Annual, Fortnightly, Tax, and Super

When you’re negotiating a job or comparing offers, knowing how an hourly rate translates to an annual salary is essential. This guide explains the standard conversion, the role of the National Minimum Wage, award rates, casual loading, and how tax and superannuation fit in. We’ll also look at the **average full time salary Australia** using the latest official data.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly to Annual

The standard calculation is straightforward: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. For full-time employees, we assume a 38-hour week, as set by the Fair Work Commission. This is the ordinary hours for most awards. For example:

- $26.44 per hour (National Minimum Wage) × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $1,004.90 per week (or $1,004.90 weekly) × 52 = $52,254.80 per year (before tax).

If you’re paid fortnightly, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. For the minimum wage, that’s $2,009.80 per fortnight. Many employers pay fortnightly, so it’s useful to know both figures.

Use our [the timesheet](/) to enter your base hourly rate and see the annual, fortnightly, and monthly equivalents. Remember, this assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal floor. From 1 July 2026, it’s $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week, as confirmed by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees get a 25% loading, making the casual rate $33.05 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave.

However, most employees are covered by an award or enterprise agreement that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award has specific pay rates that may be above the minimum. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides pay guides for each award. Always check the applicable award to ensure you’re being paid correctly.

### Average Full Time Salary Australia

To understand where your pay sits compared to others, look at the **average full time salary Australia** figures from the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS). According to the ABS Average Weekly Earnings for May 2026, full-time adult ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week. That equates to an annual salary of approximately $108,352.40 (based on 52 weeks). This is significantly higher than the minimum wage, reflecting the mix of professional and skilled roles.

For all employees (including part-time), total average weekly earnings were $1,579.20, or about $82,118.40 annually. These figures are useful benchmarks when evaluating a job offer or negotiating a raise. Our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page provides more context on how different industries and states compare.

### Casual Loading and Superannuation

If you’re a casual employee, your hourly rate should include the 25% casual loading. When using our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) tool, never enter a rate that already includes the loading; instead, enter the base rate and check the box to add 25% on top. The loading is part of your minimum entitlement, not a bonus.

Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings. For 2026–27, the super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is not deducted from your pay; it’s an additional contribution. For example, on the minimum wage annual salary of $52,254.80, your employer would pay $6,270.58 in super (12% of $52,254.80). Our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) guide explains salary sacrificing and the contribution cap.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your annual gross salary is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For 2026–27, the tax rates for residents are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45% on excess over $190,000

Plus a Medicare levy of 2% (with reductions for low incomes). For a single person earning the average full-time salary of $108,352, the tax would be approximately $24,667 plus Medicare of $2,167, leaving a take-home pay of about $81,518. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) calculator for a precise estimate.

### Putting It All Together

Whether you’re comparing a salary offer or checking your current pay, knowing the conversion from hourly to annual is key. Start with the **average full time salary Australia** of around $108,000 to see where you stand. Remember that your actual pay may differ due to award rates, overtime, penalties, or salary packaging. Always refer to official sources like the Fair Work Ombudsman for your minimum entitlements.

Our [reference tables](/data) provide quick lookups for common rates, and the [job pay](/topics/job-pay) section helps you understand how different roles compare. For a personalised calculation, visit [the timesheet](/) and enter your base hourly rate.
